description: Full-stack observability for the Ayphr API, device fleet, accounts, billing and runtime.

panels.title: Overview
panels.description: Live headline numbers for the Ayphr API and device fleet.

panels.title: Requests / second
panels.description: Requests the API is handling each second, summed across every route.

panels.title: Data points / second
panels.description: Sensor readings written to storage each second. One reading is a single temperature, humidity or pressure value.

panels.title: Error rate
panels.description: Share of responses in the 5xx range.

panels.title: Latency p95
panels.description: 95% of requests finish faster than this. The slowest 5% take longer, so a rising line means a small number of users are waiting.

panels.title: Active devices (24h)
panels.description: Devices that uploaded at least one reading in the last 24 hours.

panels.title: Total devices
panels.description: Every device record in the database, whether it is claimed by a user or not.

panels.title: Total users
panels.description: Every user account in the database.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Seconds since the server process started. Drops to zero when the process restarts.

panels.title: 5xx / second
panels.description: Responses with a 5xx status, per second. These are requests the server failed to handle.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Share of cache lookups served from Redis. A falling ratio means more requests are reaching the database.

panels.title: Upload errors / second
panels.description: Telemetry uploads that failed, per second.

panels.title: Registrations (24h)
panels.description: New user accounts created in the last 24 hours.

panels.title: Requests in flight
panels.description: Requests being handled right now. A number that climbs and does not come back down means the server is falling behind.

panels.title: CPU utilisation
panels.description: CPU time used by the server, measured in cores. A value of 2 means the server is doing two cores' worth of work.

panels.title: Memory utilisation
panels.description: Resident memory the process is holding, in bytes. This covers the JavaScript heap and everything around it.

panels.title: Event loop lag p99
panels.description: How late the event loop runs its timers, at the 99th percentile. High values mean the server is too busy to respond on time.

panels.title: HTTP
panels.description: Traffic, latency and status-code behaviour across every API route.

panels.title: Latency percentiles
panels.description: Response time percentiles. p50 is the median and p99 is the slowest 1%. The average is shown for comparison but hides slow requests.

panels.title: Requests by status
panels.description: Requests per second grouped by HTTP status code.

panels.title: Requests by method
panels.description: Requests per second grouped by HTTP method.

panels.title: Traffic share by method
panels.description: Share of all requests in the selected time range, split by HTTP method.

panels.title: Busiest routes
panels.description: The ten routes handling the most requests per second.

panels.title: Latency distribution
panels.description: Requests grouped by how long they took. Brighter cells hold more requests in that time bucket.

panels.title: Response size distribution
panels.description: Responses grouped by payload size.

panels.title: Latency p95 by route
panels.description: Response time p95 for the busiest routes, so one slow route is not hidden by the rest.

panels.title: Response size p95 by route
panels.description: Response size p95 for the busiest routes.

panels.title: Status codes over time
panels.description: Each row is a status code and each column is a time bucket. The colour shows how many responses landed in that bucket.

panels.title: Errors by status class
panels.description: Colours each time bucket by the status codes seen in it. Use it to see when errors started and how long they lasted.

panels.title: Route breakdown
panels.description: Per-route request rate, 5xx rate and p95 latency in one table.

panels.title: Requests in flight (trend)
panels.description: Current requests in flight against the highest value seen in each window.

panels.title: Devices & telemetry
panels.description: Upload volume, batch shape, persistence and raw sensor distributions.

panels.title: Upload batch size distribution
panels.description: Uploads grouped by how many readings they carried.

panels.title: Average temperature
panels.description: Average temperature with the 10th and 90th percentiles, so short spikes do not stretch the scale.

panels.title: Average humidity
panels.description: Average relative humidity with the 10th and 90th percentiles.

panels.title: Average air pressure
panels.description: Average air pressure in hectopascals with the 10th and 90th percentiles.

panels.title: Temperature distribution
panels.description: Temperature readings grouped into buckets.

panels.title: Humidity distribution
panels.description: Humidity readings grouped into buckets.

panels.title: Devices registered (24h)
panels.description: Devices paired to an account in the last 24 hours.

panels.title: Claim tokens created (24h)
panels.description: Claim codes generated so a device can be paired to an account.

panels.title: Claims completed (24h)
panels.description: Claim codes that were redeemed in the last 24 hours.

panels.title: Upload errors (24h)
panels.description: Telemetry uploads that failed in the last 24 hours.

panels.title: Points persisted (24h)
panels.description: Sensor readings written to storage in the last 24 hours.

panels.title: Avg batch size
panels.description: Average number of readings per upload.

panels.title: Accounts & auth
panels.description: Registrations, logins, sessions and rate-limit pressure.

panels.title: Auth events (24h)
panels.description: Successful registrations and logins over the last 24 hours.

panels.title: Session lifecycle
panels.description: Sessions created and destroyed per second. The gap between them is roughly the number of people logged in.

panels.title: Rate limit decisions
panels.description: Requests allowed and blocked for each rate limiter.

panels.title: Staff actions (24h)
panels.description: Staff moderation actions over the last 24 hours.

panels.title: Punishments (24h)
panels.description: Punishments issued and lifted over the last 24 hours.

panels.title: Registrations by country
panels.description: Registrations grouped by country. The country comes from the request IP, so it is approximate.

panels.title: Registration map
panels.description: Registration counts placed on a world map by country. The location comes from the request IP, so it is approximate.

panels.title: Profile & avatar activity
panels.description: Profile field edits and avatar changes per second.

panels.title: Billing
panels.description: Stripe webhook traffic and subscription funnel activity.

panels.title: Stripe webhook events by type
panels.description: Stripe webhook calls grouped by event type.

panels.title: Stripe webhook errors by type
panels.description: Stripe webhook calls that failed, grouped by event type.

panels.title: Checkout failures (24h)
panels.description: Failed checkout and billing portal attempts in the last 24 hours.

panels.title: Subscription events (24h)
panels.description: Subscription events over the last 24 hours, including checkout and auto-renew changes.

panels.title: Cache & MongoDB
panels.description: Redis cache effectiveness and MongoDB workload.

panels.title: Cache operations by result
panels.description: Redis reads and writes split by hit, miss and error.

panels.title: Cache hit ratio
panels.description: Share of cache lookups served from Redis. A falling ratio means more requests are reaching the database.

panels.title: Cache errors
panels.description: Cache reads and writes that failed.

panels.title: Mongo operations by type
panels.description: Database commands per second, grouped by operation type.

panels.title: Runtime
panels.description: Process health exported by the Prometheus default metrics.

panels.title: Event loop lag
panels.description: How late the event loop runs its timers. p99 is the worst 1% of delays and is the one to watch.

panels.title: GC duration by kind
panels.description: Time spent collecting garbage, grouped by kind and bucket.

panels.title: File descriptors
panels.description: Open file and socket handles against the process limit. Close to the limit, new connections start to fail.

panels.title: Active handles & requests
panels.description: Work the runtime has open right now, such as sockets, timers and pending requests.

panels.title: Heap spaces
panels.description: Memory used and available inside each JavaScript heap space.

title: ayphr Server
